links.comparator_used: Standard general-purpose model GPT-4 (and the domain-specific Llama3-OpenBioLLM-70B), all prompted with the same multi-agent strategy
links.outcome: Median normalized expert-rated score on open-ended complex cardiac surgery reasoning tasks (15 scenarios, 10-dimension weighted framework)
links.effect: Median normalized scores: O1 0.896, O3-mini-high 0.854, DeepSeek-R1 0.792 vs GPT-4 0.667 and Llama3-OpenBioLLM-70B 0.521; relative rankings stable across scenarios
links.tradeoff: Even the reasoning-optimized models were weak on patient safety (0.507), hallucination avoidance (0.549) and clinical efficiency (0.597) across models. Evaluators over-accepted plausible but incorrect or harmful model reasoning: 7.57% of ratings were revised from affirmative to negative after seeing the reference answers.
links.quote: Reasoning-optimized LLMs outperformed all other models.

design_hint: expert review with reference answers (human oversight of LLM output)
